topicName: The Earth and the Solar System
description: An introduction to the solar system, the sun and the planets, and the shape, movements and effects of the Earth such as day and night, seasons, time zones and eclipses.

mcq.questionText: Which star is at the centre of our solar system?
mcq.explanation: The Sun is the star at the centre of the solar system, and all the planets orbit around it.

mcq.questionText: How many planets are there in our solar system?
mcq.explanation: There are eight planets in the solar system, ranging from Mercury nearest the Sun to Neptune farthest away.

mcq.questionText: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
mcq.explanation: Mercury is the planet nearest to the Sun and the smallest planet in the solar system.

mcq.questionText: What is the true shape of the Earth best described as?

options.text: A geoid (slightly flattened at the poles)

mcq.explanation: The Earth is a geoid: nearly spherical but slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator.

mcq.questionText: The spinning of the Earth on its own axis is called what?
mcq.explanation: Rotation is the turning of the Earth on its axis, which takes about 24 hours and causes day and night.

mcq.questionText: How long does the Earth take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
mcq.explanation: The Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days (one year) to revolve once around the Sun.

mcq.questionText: What is the main cause of day and night on Earth?

options.text: The revolution of the Earth around the Sun
The rotation of the Earth on its axis
The tilt of the Earth's axis

mcq.explanation: As the Earth rotates, the side facing the Sun experiences day while the side facing away experiences night.

mcq.questionText: The four seasons experienced in many parts of the world are mainly caused by which two factors?

options.text: Rotation of the Earth and the phases of the Moon
The tilt of the Earth's axis and its revolution around the Sun
The size of the Sun and the distance of the Moon
Time zones and lines of longitude

mcq.explanation: Seasons result from the tilt of the Earth's axis (about 23.5 degrees) combined with its revolution around the Sun.

mcq.questionText: Lines drawn on a map running from east to west and measuring distance north or south of the Equator are called what?
mcq.explanation: Lines of latitude (parallels) run east-west and measure how far a place is north or south of the Equator.

mcq.questionText: Which line of longitude is taken as 0 degrees and passes through Greenwich?
mcq.explanation: The Prime Meridian is the 0 degree line of longitude passing through Greenwich, used as the starting point for measuring longitude.

mcq.questionText: The natural satellite that orbits the Earth is the:
mcq.explanation: The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite and it revolves around the Earth.

mcq.questionText: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
mcq.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because of the reddish iron oxide (rust) that covers much of its surface.

mcq.questionText: An eclipse of the Sun (solar eclipse) occurs when:

options.text: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
The Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon

mcq.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth, blocking the Sun's light from reaching part of the Earth.

mcq.questionText: The largest planet in the solar system is:
mcq.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, far bigger than all the other planets.

mcq.questionText: The Earth is divided into how many main time zones, each separated by about 15 degrees of longitude?
mcq.explanation: The Earth has 24 main time zones because it rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, giving 15 degrees of longitude per hour.

fib.questionText: The group of the Sun, planets and other bodies moving around it is called the _____ system.
fib.explanation: The solar system is made up of the Sun and all the objects that orbit it, including the planets.

fib.questionText: The planet on which we live is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known planet with life.

fib.questionText: The movement of the Earth around the Sun is called _____.
fib.explanation: Revolution is the journey of the Earth around the Sun, which takes about one year.

fib.questionText: The imaginary line around which the Earth spins is called its _____.
fib.explanation: The axis is an imaginary line passing through the North and South Poles around which the Earth rotates.

fib.questionText: The imaginary line that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The Equator is the 0 degree line of latitude that divides the Earth into two equal halves.

fib.questionText: Lines of longitude that run from the North Pole to the South Pole are also called _____.
fib.explanation: Meridians are the lines of longitude that join the two poles and measure distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.

fib.questionText: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in about _____ hours.
fib.explanation: One full rotation of the Earth takes approximately 24 hours, giving us one day and one night.

fib.questionText: When the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, a lunar _____ occurs.
fib.explanation: A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth blocks the Sun's light from reaching the Moon.

fib.questionText: The amount of tilt of the Earth's axis from the vertical is about _____ degrees.
fib.explanation: The Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5 degrees, which is responsible for the changing seasons.

fib.questionText: The hot ball of burning gases that gives the solar system light and heat is the _____.
fib.explanation: The Sun is a star made of hot gases that provides light and heat to the planets.

tf.questionText: The Sun is a planet that orbits the Earth.
tf.explanation: The Sun is a star, not a planet, and the Earth orbits the Sun, not the other way round.

tf.questionText: The Earth rotates from west to east.
tf.explanation: The Earth rotates from west to east, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west.

tf.questionText: Day and night are caused by the revolution of the Earth around the Sun.
tf.explanation: Day and night are caused by the rotation of the Earth on its axis, not by its revolution around the Sun.

tf.questionText: The Moon is the natural satellite of the Earth.
tf.explanation: The Moon is the only natural satellite of the Earth and revolves around it.

tf.questionText: All lines of latitude are equal in length.
tf.explanation: Lines of latitude differ in length; the Equator is the longest, and they get shorter towards the poles.

tf.questionText: The Equator is the longest line of latitude on the Earth.
tf.explanation: The Equator is the longest parallel of latitude, marked as 0 degrees, dividing the Earth into two hemispheres.

tf.questionText: The Earth is perfectly round like a football.
tf.explanation: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it is a geoid, slightly flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator.

tf.questionText: Places east of the Prime Meridian are ahead in time compared to places at Greenwich.
tf.explanation: Because the Earth rotates from west to east, places east of Greenwich see the Sun earlier and are ahead in time.

tf.questionText: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth.
tf.explanation: During a solar eclipse, the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth, blocking the Sun's light.

tf.questionText: The tilt of the Earth's axis has no effect on the seasons.
tf.explanation: The tilt of the Earth's axis is one of the main causes of the seasons as the Earth revolves around the Sun.

summary.correctAnswer: The Sun together with the planets and other bodies that orbit it.
summary.explanation: It includes the Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

summary.questionText: Order of the planets from the Sun
summary.correctAnswer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
summary.explanation: Mercury is nearest the Sun and Neptune is farthest.

summary.questionText: What is rotation of the Earth?
summary.correctAnswer: The spinning of the Earth on its own axis in about 24 hours.

summary.questionText: What is revolution of the Earth?
summary.correctAnswer: The movement of the Earth around the Sun in about 365 and a quarter days.
summary.explanation: Revolution, with the axial tilt, causes the seasons.

summary.correctAnswer: The rotation of the Earth on its axis.
summary.explanation: The side facing the Sun has day; the side away has night.

summary.correctAnswer: The tilt of the Earth's axis combined with its revolution around the Sun.
summary.explanation: Different parts receive different amounts of sunlight during the year.

summary.correctAnswer: Imaginary east-west lines measuring distance north or south of the Equator.
Imaginary north-south lines measuring distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.
summary.explanation: The Prime Meridian is 0 degrees longitude.

summary.correctAnswer: The natural satellite that orbits the Earth.
summary.explanation: It reflects sunlight and has no light of its own.

summary.correctAnswer: The blocking of light when the Sun, Earth and Moon line up.
summary.explanation: A solar eclipse blocks the Sun; a lunar eclipse blocks light to the Moon.

hoq.questionText: A football match in London (near Greenwich, 0 degrees) starts at 3:00 p.m. local time. At what local time should viewers in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (about 45 degrees east) watch it begin?
hoq.explanation: Each 15 degrees of longitude equals one hour, so 45 degrees east is 3 hours ahead: 3:00 p.m. plus 3 hours gives 6:00 p.m.

hoq.questionText: If the Earth suddenly stopped rotating on its axis but kept revolving around the Sun, what would most likely happen?

options.text: One side would have a very long day and the other a very long night
The Earth would become a perfect sphere
There would be no more years

hoq.explanation: Day and night come from rotation, so without it the side facing the Sun would stay in daylight while the other side stayed dark.

hoq.questionText: Two towns lie on the same line of longitude but one is near the Equator and the other is far north. Why is the northern town's noon Sun usually lower in the sky for most of the year?

options.text: Because it is closer to the Sun
Because the Earth rotates faster there
Because the curved, tilted Earth means sunlight strikes higher latitudes at a slanting angle
Because it is on a different time zone

hoq.explanation: Due to the Earth's curvature and axial tilt, the Sun's rays hit higher latitudes at a more slanting angle, so the Sun appears lower in the sky.
